definition: The Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI, pronounced "gee-pay") is an international initiative established to guide the responsible development and use of artificial intelligence (AI) in a manner that respects human rights and the shared democratic values of its members.
details: The partnership was first proposed by Canada and France at the 2018 44th G7 summit, and officially launched in June 2020. GPAI is hosted by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). GPAI seeks to bridge the gap between theory and practice by supporting research and applied activities in areas that are directly relevant to policymakers in the realm of AI. It brings together experts from industry, civil society, governments, and academia to collaborate on the challenges and opportunities presented by artificial intelligence.

explainer.lead: The Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence, or GPAI, is an international partnership for guiding AI development and use responsibly. It matters because it connects experts from different sectors with questions that matter to policymakers, while grounding its work in human rights and democratic values.

tiers.eli5: GPAI is like a club where countries and different kinds of experts work together on helpful rules and ideas for AI. Canada and France suggested it, and it began in June 2020. Its goal is to help AI grow in ways that treat people fairly and respect their rights.
tiers.practitioner: GPAI is not a software framework or an engineering standard; it is a forum for research and applied activities relevant to AI policy. Engineers may encounter its work through collaborations involving government, industry, academia, and civil society. Its practical focus is connecting technical questions with responsible development, human rights, and democratic values.
tiers.paperLevel: GPAI is formally an international initiative established to guide responsible AI development and use in accordance with human rights and members' shared democratic values. Proposed by Canada and France at the 2018 44th G7 summit and launched in June 2020, it is hosted by the OECD. Its stated method is to bridge theory and practice through policy-relevant research and applied activities conducted by cross-sector experts.
